text:
maria: heads up — since the vpc-peering change in ap-south we've seen a bunch of GPU nodes fail onboarding. keystore decrypt errors in the node logs. noticed ~30% fewer nodes able to join the warm pool this morning :facepalm:

sunil: saw that, digging. early signal points to the privatelink->peer hop hitting an SNI inspection box in that colo. TLS handshake to keystore is getting reset, KMS decrypt fails.

aj: can you paste the error from the node agent?

maria: sure — from `node-attach-xyz`:
```
2025-11-18T03:12:41Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer
2025-11-18T03:12:41Z WARN  onboarding: node join failed, retrying
```

sunil: that stack matches SNI middlebox termination — it rewrites the TLS SNI and our keystore service rejects the cert. The peering change altered the egress path, introduced a transparent proxy in the path.

ellie: ugh. That proxy was recently enabled for compliance scanning in that region. Did we whitelist keystore endpoints?

sunil: not for the peered route. It only has the shared-subnet whitelist for default nat path. Peered traffic got classified and sent through the inspection cluster.

aj: short-term mitigations: 1) revert the peering change (quick but disruptive), 2) add L7 pass-through for keystore FQDN on the proxy, or 3) route keystore egress for node-subnet via existing NAT which is already whitelisted. Any cost tradeoffs on 3? NAT egress for onboarding traffic will add data-transfer + nat gateway hours.

maria: option 3 seems minimal blast radius. We estimate onboarding traffic ~200GB/day for region peak — nat costs ~ $0.045/GB + gw hour charges. rough daily delta ~ $9-10.

ellie: we should also consider audit logging completeness — the proxy does audit tap and we rely on that for compliance. routing via NAT will drop that enriched scan. Compliance might push back.

sunil: true. If we route via NAT, we lose the inspection telemetry. Alternative: ask the compliance team to add explicit allow for `keystore.internal.redwood` in their proxy rules for the peered path — keeps audit and fixes joins. That needs their signoff but is ideal.

aj: do we have an IAM/KMS conditional that restricts decryption by source IPs? Could tighten/loosen temporarily?

maria: KMS key policy is fine but keystore proxy adds auth based on source zone. Keystore validates the client cert + SNI. So the proxy breaking SNI is the root cause, not KMS policy.

ellie: action plan suggestion: 1) add temporary nat route for node-subnet -> natgw (owner: aj, ETA 30m) 2) open compliance ticket to add SNI passthrough for keystore FQDN on the inspection cluster (owner: sunil -> cc @compliance) 3) monitor metric: warm-pool join success rate and keystore decrypt errors (owner: maria) 4) cost check after 24h and revert if >2x expected (owner: ellie).

aj: I'll push the route change now. command I will run: `ip route replace 10.0.32.0/24 via natgw-xyz table nodes` and update route53 solve if necessary.

ops-bot: deploy queued: route-update-nodes -> up to 2m for propagation. Triggered by aj.

maria: thanks. after route flip, nodes started joining almost immediately. join rate went from 67% -> 98% in 12m.

sunil: filed compliance ticket CL-2025-381, requested passthrough for `keystore.internal.redwood` on peered path. noted urgency + audit retention needs.

ellie: good. cost watch: provisioning did add ~11GB egress in first hour — looks in line with estimate. I'll own the 24h cost report.

aj: follow-up question — do we want a longer-term fix? options: a) ensure peering path preserves SNI (preferred), b) make keystore tolerant to missing SNI by falling back to cert pinning (risky), c) route keystore traffic to a dedicated endpoint that avoids inspection. Thoughts?

sunil: prefer a) or c). a) needs infra+compliance change but preserves audit. c) would be a platform change but gives explicit operational control. both require design doc.

maria: agree — moving to postmortem + action item to draft RFC for dedicated keystore egress endpoint (owner: maria). Also note: log a compliance exception if we keep NAT route for >48h.

ellie: I'll coordinate exception if needed.

maria: final — immediate fix applied, monitoring green, compliance ticket opened, RFC for long-term strategy next week. closing thread once RFC is live. :white_check_mark:
